Run BayesSpace spatial clustering

runBayesSpace.Rd

Runs BayesSpace (Zhao et al. 2021) spatial clustering on the counts and spot positions of a giotto object and stores:

  • cell metadata <name> (BayesSpace's spatial cluster) and <name>_init (the initial non-spatial clustering);

  • when BayesSpace preprocesses the counts (dim_reduction_name = NULL), its PCA as dimension reduction <name>_pca (method "pca"), with its highly variable features in misc$hvf.

The spot grid comes from cell metadata columns array_row and array_col when present, otherwise from the spatial locations and the spot spacing. Enhanced (subspot) resolution, spatialEnhance(), is not wrapped. If you use it, please cite the original paper (see bayesspaceParam()).

Usage

runBayesSpace(
  gobject,
  param,
  spat_unit = NULL,
  feat_type = NULL,
  expression_values = "raw",
  dim_reduction_name = NULL,
  spat_loc_name = "raw",
  name = "bayesspace",
  verbose = NULL
)

Arguments

gobject

giotto object

param

a bayesspaceParam() (needs q)

spat_unit, feat_type

spatial unit and feature type

expression_values

expression values with the counts

dim_reduction_name

optional name of a stored PCA (cells x dimensions) to cluster on instead of BayesSpace's own preprocessing

spat_loc_name

name of the spatial locations

name

name of the results

verbose

be verbose

Value

The giotto object with the results.

References

Zhao E, Stone MR, Ren X, Guenthoer J, Smythe KS, Pulliam T, Williams SR, Uytingco CR, Taylor SEB, Nghiem P, Bielas JH, Gottardo R. Spatial transcriptomics at subspot resolution with BayesSpace. Nature Biotechnology 39, 1375-1384 (2021). doi:10.1038/s41587-021-00935-2

See also

bayesspaceParam()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
g <- GiottoData::loadGiottoMini("visium")
g <- runBayesSpace(g, param = bayesspaceParam(q = 7))
} # }
